text:
Two teams searching for footing meet at Madison Square Garden. The Rangers are 1-4-0 in their last five but snapped a four-game winless run with a 3-1 win over STL two days ago. The Flyers are 1-3-1 over the same stretch after a 4-2 loss to MIN, and they're without Rasmus Ristolainen.

Our numbers give NYR the edge in how the games have been played. At five on five, the Rangers have taken 52% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality), against 40% for PHI. We project 3.23 goals for New York and 2.85 for Philadelphia. The Flyers also take 4.3 penalties a game, which keeps handing out power plays. In net, Dan Vladar (projected) is at -0.23 goals saved above expected this season (how many goals he's stopped beyond what the shots called for), though he was +12.74 last year. James Reimer (projected) is at -1.96 after one start, with the Rangers missing Igor Shesterkin, who is on injured reserve.

Matvei Michkov has 11 points in his last ten games, and we have him at 28% to score. Trevor Zegras, also 28%, has a homecoming angle, since he was born in Bedford. For New York, Alexis Lafrenière is at 32%. Our under-the-radar pick is Pavel Dorofeyev, a third-liner with 4.5 expected goals in his last 10 games, at 31% to score. He's a player to watch, not a lock.
